subject: Business
title: The Value Proposition Canvas
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Value Proposition Canvas.

hook.text: Your product has 50 features. Customers use three. You're solving problems they don't have.

buildup.text: The value proposition canvas maps customer jobs, pains, and gains against your product's offerings.

discovery.text: Fit happens when your pain relievers match their pains and your gain creators match their desired gains.

twist.text: Most startups design features they find exciting instead of features customers actually need.

climax.text: Slack didn't sell 'team messaging.' It sold 'less email.' The pain was what mattered.

punchline.text: Don't list what you built. Describe what pain you kill.

quiz.question: What does the value proposition canvas map?
options: Customer pains and gains against your product's offerings

details.summary: The Value Proposition Canvas maps customer jobs, pains, and gains on one side against your products, pain relievers, and gain creators on the other. Fit is achieved when your offering addresses the most important jobs and resolves the most critical pains customers experience.
details.whyItMatters: The canvas provides a structured method for ensuring products actually solve real customer problems. It prevents the common pitfall of building products based on assumptions rather than validated customer needs, reducing product-market fit risk.
takeaways: The customer profile maps jobs, pains, and gains from the customer perspective
The value map describes how your offering addresses those customer needs
Fit means your pain relievers and gain creators match priority customer needs

faq.question: How do you use the Value Proposition Canvas in practice?
faq.answer: Start by interviewing customers to fill the customer profile with real data. Map their most important jobs, worst pains, and most desired gains. Then design your value proposition to address the highest-priority items. Test fit through prototyping and customer feedback.

faq.question: What is the most common mistake when using this canvas?
faq.answer: Filling the customer profile with assumptions rather than data from actual customer conversations. Teams often project their own beliefs about what customers want. Effective use requires direct customer research to validate every element of the customer profile before designing solutions.
